findings.cause: The first registry render exposed selectable provider buttons before the passive initial-ID pin. An actual click could enqueue an explicit target, then the old effect assigned the default ID and overwrote it.
findings.proof: Original provider-multi single-file rerun passed 9/9, so a lucky rerun was not accepted as disproof. A controlled initial Promise plus actual createRoot and MutationObserver delivered exactly one native DOM click at first button publication, without mocking React hooks or adding delays. The unchanged source ended at ChatGPT and failed; functional pin passes the same probe.
findings.repair: Pin using setSelectedId(previous => previous || effectiveId), retaining any user choice already queued. Added formal first-publication regressions for both a new provider and an existing alternative; neither starts a mutation.
findings.prevention: Whenever a default is applied after async publication, preserve a concurrently explicit selection. Exercise first observable DOM interaction with a controlled load, not just post-effect stable state.

findings.cause: Settings is now loaded on demand. The old tests queried child buttons synchronously and one retained the fallback Dialog container, which is replaced by the real Settings dialog. Auth expiry was also injected before the Settings module finished mounting.
findings.repair: Wait for the actual desired Settings navigation control, then trigger expiry/navigation and capture the current dialog. Updated analogous App settings entrypoints that previously happened to share a warmed module. Preserved draft bytes, unknown receipt, no replay, unmounted ownership and renewed-login assertions.
findings.prevention: Lazy entrypoint changes require actual App consumers in addition to a DeferredPanel unit test. Await a readiness control and reacquire replaced ownership containers; never add sleeps or rely on test order warming imports.

findings.cause: The integration fixture throws at fetch, but the real Api.call now maps that exception to a safe localized transport_error. The first stale raw-English expectation concealed later obsolete assumptions: automation effort displays localized labels, and same-scope refresh retains rows while rereading every already-loaded page.
findings.repair: Assert the actionable transport message and absence of the raw exception, retain previous rows/retry checks, assert highest label has max transport value and exact effort option values. Hold the refreshed second-page Promise to verify original Beta/max remains visible while submission is disabled, then restore only after completion. Remove Beta on a later complete refresh to verify unavailable state, no Alpha fallback and no submission, then restore and assert exact provider/model/effort request.
findings.prevention: Read and execute the entire compound consumer scenario after the first failure is repaired. Use controlled page promises for loading admission; preserve option transport values independently of labels and preserve actual parameter assertions.

findings.cause: The removed-model test began with no stored reasoning effort, edited a draft to max, then cleared it. Returning to the original unset value now correctly removes a no-op change; the old test incorrectly demanded a null mutation.
findings.repair: Assert zero changes and no RPC even on forced form submission. Add a separate persisted-max case that refreshes to a missing model, retains the current value, then explicitly clears and submits exactly one null change with the expected configuration version.
findings.prevention: Separate undoing a draft from clearing an already-persisted setting; cover both actual states rather than weakening no-op suppression.

findings.cause: History intentionally formats full dates using zh-CN; the test used the host default locale. Windows default happened to agree, while Linux returned English month/day and AM/PM.
findings.repair: Expected dates explicitly use zh-CN. Full-date ordering of failed attempt and retry, receipt closure, accepted/error state and absence of RPC remain asserted.
findings.prevention: Assertions must use the declared product locale, never unspecified host locale; retain Linux and Windows evidence.

whyEarlierChecksMissed: The earlier narrowly chosen UI regression sets did not exercise all final App-level lazy consumers and the whole real-API automation scenario together. The broad selector includes these consumers, but the manually selected subsets and static full audits did not expose the stale assertions before the matrix.

Initial provider pin coverage checked removal/default changes after initialization, not an explicit selection at first registry DOM publication. The ordinary test passed in an isolated rerun and on Linux; the controlled boundary probe was necessary to establish the real race.

A first failing expectation stops later assertions in a compound case. Once safe transport text was fixed, localized effort and retained-pagination assumptions also required explicit reconciliation against current behavior.
Local host locale masked the history expectation mismatch. Platform coverage remains required; Windows-only success is not evidence for unspecified locale assumptions.
